title: Extension manifest
description: persona-extension.json (read as persona-plugin.json before the rename, #1844) at the root of an extension's package. The hub reads it strictly: a field it does not know anywhere fails the install. Rules a schema cannot say (a gate file inside the package, ids unique across extensions, version ranges) stay the hub's.

Host.description: A host name, lowercase, no scheme, port or path; *. may start it.

tags.description: What the market shows and searches (docs "Extension market"): at most 16, each 1 to 24 characters. Packages and indexes carry the manifest without them (hubs before tags refuse an unknown field); the index entry carries them instead.

off_by_default.description: Contributions ("<point>/<id>") that start switched off: at install, and at an upgrade the ones the version before did not have (docs "Contribution switches"). Not a connector or a channel bound to one (their switch is the connector's). Hubs before it refuse the manifest.

depends.description: Extensions it needs installed and on (docs "Dependencies"): while one is missing, off or too old it waits in needs_setup.

extension_pack.description: An extension pack (docs "Extension packs"): installing it installs these. A pack has no runtime and no contributes of its own.

configuration.description: The configuration's JSON Schema, in the subset every app draws as a form (docs "Configuration: the form subset").

tools.description: Command-line programs the hub installs into the extension's own directory and puts first on its PATH (docs "Command-line programs (tools)", #4507). Installing them is a permission. Hubs before them refuse the manifest.

ToolSpec.description: One command-line program. Exactly one of archive and npm.

requires.description: Other tools of the manifest installed (and on PATH) first.

ToolCheck.description: A copy on the hub's PATH (outside the home directory) is used instead of installing one when <name> <args> prints a version (the first x.y.z) of at least min_version.

ToolArchive.description: A download: a .tar.gz, .tgz or .zip with the program at path, or the program itself.

ToolNPM.description: An npm package unpacked as published: no install scripts, no dependencies (a bundled package).

bin.description: The key of package.json's bin; default the tool's name.

AuthSpec.description: The extension signs in: its program answers auth.status, auth.step and auth.logout (docs "Sign-in (auth)").

page.description: An extension_page (plugin_page) ui contribution: its own sign-in page for apps that do not know auth; apps that do leave it out of its pages.

version.description: A range of its versions: >=1.2.0, <2.0.0, or both with a space between.

Exports.description: Extension points it opens to other extensions: they contribute under contributes["<this id>.<point id>"] and depend on it.

schema.description: Each contribution's JSON Schema, in the configuration's subset (docs "Configuration: the form subset"); id is always there and required.

market.description: The address of the market it comes from (github:owner/repo, https://…), as the hub registered it; empty: the pack's own market, else the first registered market that has it.

version.description: A range of its versions, as in depends.

Engines.description: What the extension runs on. extension_protocol is plugin_protocol's new name; a hub reads either.

persona.description: A range of hub build numbers (">=202611050000 <202701010000").

Resources.description: The most a program may use when the hub runs it in a sandbox (docs/extensions.md "Sandbox"): memory in MB, CPU in percent of one core. Unset: 1024 MB, 100%.

Command.description: A path in the package, or one per platform ({"linux-amd64": "bin/x"}).

NodeRuntime.description: The extension's program on computers (docs/extensions.md "Programs running on computers"): one per platform (darwin-* / linux-*), on the machines picked in the configuration field `machines` (an array of format machine, x-os the programs' systems).

NodePermissions.description: What the program on computers asks for there: hosts it reaches, files outside its data directory, macOS's privacy permissions.

Permissions.description: A closed vocabulary: a permission the hub does not know fails the install.

hub_api.description: The old way: the hub's full token. With hub scopes, the scopes win.

hub.description: The scopes of the hub's API it calls: its token opens their routes only.

gh_login.description: It asks the hub for the GitHub token of a computer's gh login (the one the user picks for the GitHub connector), held in its memory only.

usage_gateways.description: It reads the account list of the account-pool gateways in the hub's usage sources (usage.gateway_accounts): accounts, status and quota windows, never a key.

agent_runtimes.description: Its program is an agent runtime that connects to this machine's node; in a sandbox it gets a socket in its run directory (PERSONA_RUNTIME_SOCKET) that leads to the node's runtime.sock only. Needs runtime.

error_reports.description: It receives the error and crash reports of the hub and the user's devices, scrubbed (no message text, tokens, user names, machine names or IP addresses). Needed by contributes.error_reports.

Contributes.description: Contributions by extension point. A point this hub does not know installs with a warning, not taking effect.

SkillItem.description: A skill (docs "Declarative contributions"): a directory of the package with SKILL.md, put in with the assistant's skills.

dir.description: The directory, relative to the package.

PromptItem.description: A prompt: instructions (a .md of the package added to the assistant's CLAUDE.md) or quick (a template the apps offer in the message box).

text.description: quick: what goes into the message box.

ThemeColors.description: A scheme's role colors, #RRGGBB: accent (required), positive, caution, danger, ai.

ThemeItem.description: A theme (Theme Color): the design system's role colors for light and dark; the apps check the contrast and do not offer one that fails.

LookID.description: A look's id: also a persona package's (the apps cache by it).

BuiltinLook.description: A look every app draws itself: Mochi (the default), Visor, Circuit.

LookTexts.description: A text in the other languages, by code (docs/i18n.md): only zh-Hans, en and ja, each 1 to 40 characters (the hub checks).

LookAvatarDark.description: The face on dark backgrounds; what it leaves out is the light one's.

sizes.description: Side in pixels → a square PNG of the package.

svg.description: An SVG of the package (the hub cleans it).

LookAvatar.description: The face: square PNGs by their side in pixels (16 to 1024, at least one), an SVG, and the same for dark mode.

sizes.description: Side in pixels → a square PNG of the package.

svg.description: An SVG of the package (the hub cleans it: no scripts, nothing from outside it).

safe.description: The share of the circle what matters stays inside.

LookPalette.description: An appearance's colors, #RRGGBB (docs/persona.md "Palettes", the apps' PersonaPalette).

file.description: An APNG (or a still PNG) of the package.

LookDotStates.description: The dot's states; idle is required.

LookDot.description: The animated dot in the Persona tab's top bar; without it the hub takes the largest avatar PNG as idle.

LookItem.description: A look (docs/extensions.md "Looks"): Persona's name, face, colors and dot, served as a persona package. app_icon_fallback is the built-in icon used where only the app's own icons can be shown.

TriageTemplateItem.description: A template of an inbox source's triage rules (triage_rules): settings offer it.

ErrorReportsItem.description: It is given the error and crash reports of the hub and the user's devices (error_reports.deliver): needs the program to speak the protocol, on_startup and permissions.error_reports.

sources.description: Only reports from these; omitted: all.

TunnelItem.description: A tunnel the apps can reach this hub through when its own addresses do not answer (docs "In-app tunnels"): an in-app tunnel core built into the app, going to the configuration's target_host and target_port.

AgentFilterItem.description: Agent sessions kept out of Agents (docs "Agent filters"): a session goes when it is one of agents and any of the matchers fits it.

title.description: What the extension's contributions list calls it.

when.description: A boolean field of the configuration: the filter holds only while it is true, and that field is its only switch. Without it the filter holds while the extension is on.

agents.description: Whose sessions: Claude Code, Codex; none: both.

originators.description: Codex: session_meta.originator of the rollout, exactly.

added_dirs.description: Claude Code: a directory the session was given besides its own (additionalWorkingDirectories), this or under it; ~/ is the home directory.

first_message_prefixes.description: The first user message starts with one of these (leading blanks ignored): a fallback for sessions without a marker.

NamedItem.description: A contribution with only an id and a name: voice, computer, browser.

MCPServerItem.description: An MCP server for the Claude assistant (docs "MCP servers"): a command line on the assistant's machine, its tools as mcp__<id>__<tool>. The command reads its own configuration; Persona adds nothing to its environment. Not a shell or an interpreter.

id.description: The server's name for the assistant; not jarvis or persona.

command.description: Looked up on PATH, then in ~/bin.

env.description: A PERSONA_ variable (JARVIS_ read too) that, when set, replaces the lookup: a path, or "" / 0 / off / false to leave the server out.

requires.description: Words `<command> --help` must print; otherwise the server is left out.

deny.description: Tools never callable. Any other tool goes by the conversation's permission mode.

UIItem.description: A place in the apps the extension draws (docs "UI slots").

opens.description: overview_card, capsule_card and widget only: a nav_page or extension_page of the same extension.

connector.description: inbox_item only: one of the extension's own connectors.

families.description: widget only (and needed there): the sizes it can be drawn at.

refresh_minutes.description: widget only: how often the widget is drawn again on its own (30 when not said).

ShortcutItem.description: An action of the extension the system runs (docs "System placements"): Shortcuts and Siri on iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch. The hub asks the extension shortcut.run with the values.

ui.description: A whole page of the same extension (nav_page or extension_page) the app opens to show more of the result.

ShortcutParam.description: A value the shortcut asks for; it reaches the extension as a string (a toggle's "true" / "false").
